clue.text: Artlessness of dog going round and round

indicators.note: the dog goes round the next pieces, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dog chasing its tail, round and round, without guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Candour is frankness and openness, the opposite of guile, so it can stand for artlessness.

clue.text: Leader is tricky chap, predominantly ill disposed at heart

indicators.note: the second piece is put in the middle of the first
tricky suggests the letters of chap are twisted
disposed means arranged, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: A sly man in charge, mostly badly inclined deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'predominantly' keeps IL from ILL; 'disposed' rearranges it to LI.
explanation.definitionFit: A caliph was the ruler of a Muslim state, successor to Muhammad.

clue.text: Felt tense about screening bug

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read in reverse
the words hide the answer inside

explanation.surface: Someone tense about having an insect checked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' hides ELTTEN in 'Felt tense', which 'about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate them, as a sting from the plant does.

clue.text: Ignored, left out, bachelor enters, reserved to an embarrassing degree

indicators.note: out says the left letter is dropped
the bachelor letter comes into its place

parts.note: overlooked means ignored
B is short for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A list of snubs, departures and a bachelor turning up, all embarrassingly booked.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight or hotel is overbooked when more seats or rooms are sold than exist, an embarrassing excess of reservations.

clue.text: Opener finally hit out over leg boundary to show authority

indicators.note: take the end letter of the word
the letters of hit go over the leg letter, around it in a down clue
out means the letters of hit are put out of order
the boundary of leg is its last letter

explanation.surface: A cricket opener hitting a boundary on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is one half of the field; a boundary is a shot reaching the rope. Here they give R, an anagram of HIT, and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A right is an entitlement or power, the authority to do something.

clue.text: After sun, tanned to some extent, turned loose

indicators.note: to tan is to beat, so the word sun is knocked about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned asks for the following piece to be read backwards

parts.note: partly, so in part

explanation.surface: Someone after sunbathing, partly tanned, has turned over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is only a link, and 'tanned' means beaten, not browned: the sun is knocked about. 'to some extent' is a phrase for partly.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose is to release or set free, as unbuckling a strap releases what it holds.

clue.text: Final terms tail off amid tumult for a change

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new order
the last letter of amid is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Peace terms collapsing amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail off' cuts AMID to AMI; 'for a change' rearranges AMI and TUMULT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last demand, with consequences if refused.

clue.text: Appear right leaving simple point raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, backwards
the right letter leaves the word

parts.note: mere means simple, nothing more
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Instructions for a simple point going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes R from MERES to give MEES, which 'raised' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to appear or give the impression of being.

clue.text: Neither shower nor a drip?

parts.note: one drop of rain is too little to be a shower, yet comes from the sky rather than a tap

explanation.surface: A wet day that is neither one thing nor the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NOR A DRIP rearranged also give the answer, though no word signals the shuffle, so it is a bonus rather than the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A single drop of rain falling is less than a shower and not a leaking drip.

clue.text: Boxer dog on international register

parts.note: a pug is a small dog breed
a register is a list

explanation.surface: A boxer dog entered on the international breed register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like the dog breed but is a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pugilist is a fist fighter, from Latin pugil, a boxer.

clue.text: Supple snake shedding skin

indicators.note: losing its outer covering, so the first and last letters go, as a snake sloughs its skin

parts.note: to snake is to slither along

explanation.surface: A supple snake sloughing its skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful in movement, a close synonym of supple.

clue.text: Threatening to go out grooving?

definitions.meaning: said of a candle flame flickering and about to die
a gutter is a groove or channel, so fitting gutters or channels is making grooves

explanation.surface: Someone out dancing, threatening to leave the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle flame that flickers low is guttering; gutters are grooves, so cutting them is grooving.

clue.text: Employ both midwives taking blood

indicators.note: midwives deliver, so the letters are delivered into a new form

explanation.surface: A hospital using two midwives who also draw blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midwives' is an unusual anagram signal, read as a verb: it delivers EMPLOY BOTH in a new shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for drawing blood from a vein is a technical synonym for taking blood.

clue.text: In Miami do, ladies look for blue-eyed boy

indicators.note: the answer is held within these words

explanation.surface: At a Miami party, the ladies hunt for a favourite young man.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-eyed boy is a favourite, someone adored, much as a worshipped star is.

clue.text: Others downing beer devoured US-style spread?

indicators.note: the others swallow the beer, holding it inside

parts.note: the rest are the others
ale is beer
ate means devoured

explanation.surface: The others drink beer and eat an American-style buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' suggests food, but a spread is also a ranch or estate; this phrase is the American term for property.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call land and buildings property by this phrase, and a large ranch is a spread.

clue.text: Fashion folk wearing children's bloomers

parts.note: to forge is to fashion or shape

indicators.note: the children's word is worn around the folk, so it contains them

parts.note: tots are small children
men are people, folk

explanation.surface: Fashionable people sporting children's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like knickers but means flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: These small blue flowers are plants that bloom, so bloomers in the crossword sense.

clue.text: Could be snail trail's about to cover a pet

indicators.note: the reversed word covers the next pieces, holding them inside
the trailing word is read backwards

parts.note: to dog someone is to trail them
a pet is a fit of sulking, a strop

explanation.surface: A snail trail spreading over a household pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' is a sulk, not an animal; a strop is British slang for a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The snail is the best-known member of this class of molluscs, so an example.

clue.text: Egg producer shows way to get egg on

parts.note: St, street, is a way
to egg on is to urge on

explanation.surface: A hen-keeper's guide to coaxing out an egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish's eggs are caviar; 'egg' appears twice in different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: This large fish produces roe, sold as caviar, so it is a producer of eggs.

clue.text: Cause of depression's socially acceptable for one who's overweight?

indicators.note: the acceptable letter is put in place of the one

parts.note: dimpling forms dimples, small depressions in a surface
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Accepting that someone overweight is depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for one' swaps U for I, the one; 'one' also opens the definition. 'depression' is a hollow, not low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumpling is used affectionately of a short plump person.

clue.text: Hype co-ordinates general effect

parts.note: to hype is to tout or promote loudly
matching clothes worn together form an ensemble

explanation.surface: Marketing puffery for a range of matching outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'co-ordinates' suggests maps or graphs, but means a matching outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase, used in English, means the overall impression of something taken as a whole.

clue.text: Monster bore

definitions.meaning: to bore is to go on and on tediously, read here as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a mythical monster; split in two the letters mean to continue tediously.

clue.text: Old artist in fifties pursuing forte — could it be to do with naked ladies?

indicators.note: the fifties piece follows the music marking

parts.note: f is the music marking for forte, loud

indicators.note: the old and artist pieces go inside the fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties is LL
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An old painter in his fifties, chasing a forte for nudes.
explanation.walkthrough: Naked ladies are a flower, the autumn crocus, so the risque surface hides a botanical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to flowers, and naked ladies is a common name for some flowering bulbs.

clue.text: Delighted to hear how present's turned out

indicators.note: says the words are to be taken as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: a gift arrives in paper, wrapped

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to hear how a gift turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means wholly absorbed or enchanted, a state of delight.

clue.text: Pop charts' role to produce such music?

indicators.note: to pop is to burst, so the letters scatter and reform

explanation.surface: Asks what pop charts are for, if not producing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like the music genre but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for or played by an orchestra is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Create icy detachment with initial change of temperature, and split

indicators.note: the first letter, cold, is changed to hot, a change of temperature

parts.note: glaciers calve when ice breaks away from them

explanation.surface: Splitting with someone frostily after things warm up.
explanation.walkthrough: C (cold) becomes H (hot), as on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve is to divide into two equal parts, so to split.

clue.text: Is a chant oddly overlooked in vocal style?

indicators.note: the odd letters are ignored, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Asks whether chanting gets ignored in singing styles.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat singing uses improvised nonsense syllables, a jazz vocal style.

clue.text: Work in special building run by bishops

indicators.note: the work abbreviation goes inside the other letters
the letters of special are being built into a new structure

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Work going on in a special building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' suggests a cathedral but is the anagram signal on SPECIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An episcopal church is governed by bishops, from the Greek for overseer.

clue.text: Prophesy sounds as if it could be boring

indicators.note: the answer is heard as another word

parts.note: an auger is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: Predicting that something might be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' means making holes, not tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foretell, as Roman priests read the future from birds.

clue.text: Discredited and died following Tyneside scandal?

indicators.note: the death abbreviation comes after the other pieces

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
-gate is a suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: Someone discredited and killed after a scandal in Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something negated has been nullified or disproved, so discredited.

clue.text: Wise briefly to split up and others may be carrying on endlessly

indicators.note: the and-others abbreviation is split to take the comedian inside

parts.note: et al. is Latin, and others
Ernie Wise, the comedian, was called Ern by his partner Eric Morecambe

explanation.surface: Wise split up with Morecambe, and others may carry on for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting for ever, without end or pause.
